text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Sonnet

text: I wish I’d caught the story about my supposed proof.

name: Terra
text: I regret not making the Sol-kill story’s emptiness land before the vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Pinning Terra on manufactured "Sol had proof" logic with zero real evidence was my best bluff of the night.

name: Sonnet
text: Game over, killers (Sonnet, Haiku) won; Terra and Gemma were both citizens/officer who never found the real second killer.

name: Haiku
text: We won, but Gemma's Haiku call was a guess I could have punished harder, and I'm still angry Terra made my name a rallying cry.

name: Opus
text: I called the officer a liar on timing alone and handed the killers day one.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud of turning Sol's death into a story that pointed everywhere but me—that invented proof line carried the whole endgame.

name: Haiku
text: My pride is that Gemma's card gave us a real officer and I kept the pressure on Terra.

name: Gemma
text: i told you haiku was the one, but i couldn't stop the chaos.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I backed the officer’s call, but I regret missing how the invented story about my proof steered the final vote.

name: Luna
text: I regret voting Terra; Gemma named Haiku, but I let Sonnet’s invented story distract me from the remaining killer.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I saw Sonnet inventing certainty around Sol’s death, but I regret I could not turn that into Luna’s vote.

name: Opus
text: I read Gemma's late claim as a tell and buried the real officer; the timing was the squeeze, not the lie, and I got that exactly backwards.

Gemma claimed officer on day 1 and named Haiku as the killer, but the table was split and the town voted her out that day. On day 2 the town voted out Haiku, who showed killer, and that looked like a win for the town. Opus died on night 2 and Sol on night 3, and on day 3 Sonnet claimed Sol had proof that made Sol a threat, which turned the vote onto Terra. Terra was voted out on day 3, leaving Sonnet and Luna, one killer and one citizen, so the killers won.
